---
title: "Compatibility and limitations"
---

## PHP versions

`composer.json` requires PHP `^8.3`, which allows PHP 8.3 and later 8.x
releases. CI runs the test suite on PHP 8.3, 8.4, and 8.5. On Linux it runs
each version in five modes: without OPcache, with OPcache and no JIT, with the
tracing JIT, with `opcache.jit=1205`, and with `opcache.jit=1235`. On macOS it
runs the OPcache and `opcache.jit=1205` modes. No PHP extension is required.

## With the extension

- When the `phit` extension is loaded, the polyfill's bootstrap defines
  nothing, and every `Phit\` function is the extension's. If the loaded
  extension is older than the phit release the polyfill reproduces, the
  functions it lacks stay undefined.
- `composer.json` declares `"provide": {"ext-phit": "*"}`. Composer therefore
  treats a package that requires `ext-phit` as satisfied by the polyfill.
  `Phit\read_csv` and `Phit\CsvReader` remain unavailable without the
  extension.

## Differences from the extension

- `Phit\read_csv` and `Phit\CsvReader` are not implemented.
- The listwise-deletion warning is raised with `E_USER_WARNING` because PHP
  code cannot raise `E_WARNING`. The text is identical.
- Scalar arguments of the wrong type follow PHP's userland rules: coercion in
  non-strict files, otherwise `TypeError`. The extension raises an
  `\Exception`.
- The polyfill's functions refuse to run under OPcache's JIT, as described
  below. The extension runs under any JIT setting.
- Matrix products above 5×5 follow the extension's aarch64 build, which uses
  fused multiply-adds. On an x86-64 CPU without FMA, the extension's own
  products can differ from the polyfill's in the last bit.

## Performance

The polyfill runs the extension's algorithms in PHP. These timings were
recorded on 2026-10-28 on an Apple M5 Ultra with PHP 8.5.10, OPcache on, and
the JIT off, comparing polyfill commit `ab803fd` with phit commit `3861d77` in
one process. Each design has 10 standard normal predictors plus an intercept.

| Model | n | Polyfill | Extension |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `fit_ols` | 10,000 | 26 ms | 2.9 ms |
| `fit_ols` | 100,000 | 262 ms | 29 ms |
| `fit_logistic` | 10,000 | 160 ms | 7.0 ms |
| `fit_logistic` | 100,000 | 1.60 s | 72 ms |

The mixed models are the slowest part of the polyfill. In the recorded cases
it took 13 to 78 times as long as the extension. `fit_mixed` and `fit_lmer`
repeat a dense QR factorization at every optimizer step, so their cost grows
roughly with the cube of the number of random coefficients.

| Fit | Extension | Polyfill |
|---|---:|---:|
| `fit_mixed_intercept`, sleepstudy (n = 180) | 0.2 ms | 2.6 ms |
| `fit_logistic_mixed`, n = 185, Laplace | 1.3 ms | 26 ms |
| `fit_logistic_mixed`, n = 185, 9 quadrature points | 2.1 ms | 41 ms |
| `fit_mixed`, random slopes, 24 random coefficients | 0.7 ms | 37 ms |
| `fit_mixed`, nested, 84 random coefficients | 7.8 ms | 604 ms |
| `fit_mixed`, four nested levels, 120 random coefficients | 103 ms | 8.0 s |

The mixed-model timings were recorded on 2026-10-16 on the same machine and PHP version.

## The JIT

The polyfill runs with OPcache and without the JIT. `opcache.jit=disable` is
the default on PHP 8.4 and 8.5. PHP 8.3's defaults (`opcache.jit=tracing` with
`opcache.jit_buffer_size=0`) also leave the JIT off. Every `Phit\` function the polyfill defines
throws an exception with code 1007 while any JIT compiles the process, on
every PHP version, before it reads its arguments. The phit extension is not
affected and runs under any setting.

The JIT has computed wrong results in the polyfill without an error on all
three versions, as described below. These are PHP bugs that can affect any
PHP code; the polyfill's numerical loops trigger them. The polyfill
refuses every function, including those that have not failed, so a miscompile
the tests have not found cannot produce a wrong number either.

`Phit\Polyfill\Polyfill::implementation()` returns an implementation without
the check. The test suite uses it, and CI still runs the suite under the
tracing JIT, `opcache.jit=1205`, and `opcache.jit=1235` to record the
miscompiles.

### PHP 8.4 and 8.5

A function JIT with hot-counter triggers compiles a function while it is
running and enters the compiled code partway through a loop. In that case PHP
can lose the value of a variable that is live across the loop entry
(php-src #24214). The polyfill avoids the patterns that triggered the bug in
its own code, and its full suite passes under `opcache.jit=1235` on both
versions. Because the bug is in PHP, other code paths may still meet it.

On PHP 8.4.26 on GitHub's x86-64 runner, the tracing JIT also miscompiles the
BOBYQA optimizer behind the mixed models without any message. One reference
case ends at a minimum 18% away from the correct one. The failure has not
reproduced on other machines with the same PHP build. PHP 8.5 passes under
the tracing JIT in CI, which was also true of PHP 8.4 before this runner.

### PHP 8.3

PHP 8.3 uses an older JIT backend, and that release line receives security
fixes only. With the tracing JIT, one beta-distribution case in the stress
suite returns a value that differs from the extension's in the 12th digit
after certain functions have been compiled. With `opcache.jit=1215` or `1235`,
the PHP process crashes in the test suite.

PHP 8.3's `round()` first rounds its argument to 15 significant digits, so
`round(0.49999999999999994)` is 1.0 there. The polyfill uses its own exact
rounding, which matches Rust and PHP 8.4.

### Optimizer folding with NaN

OPcache's optimizer rewrites `!($x > 0)` as `$x <= 0`, which differs when `$x`
is NaN. The polyfill writes such conditions so that NaN takes the same branch
as in the extension, with or without OPcache, on all three versions.
